newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares rise, BUX futures surge.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares rise, BUX futures surge.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed higher for the second successive day on Tuesday but traders said they expected the market to remain rangebound as the rise was not convincing.
The BUX index closed at 5,178.13 points, up 96.56.

"The rise continued but the current increase isn't straightforward," said Balazs Bathory of Creditanstalt Securities. "Usually there's one buyer for the individual papers, thus the liquidity hasn't gone back to normal."
Another trader said the chemicals stocks were the main driving force on Tuesday.
"Mainly TVK propelled the market," said Laszlo Baranyai of Gog Securities.
TVK gained more than seven percent or 150 forints to finish at 2,220, while Borsodchem, the bourse's other chemical firm, grew more than five percent or 315 forints to end the day at 6,310.
Elsewhere on the market, many of the bourse's leading stocks finished higher.
Hotelier Danubius also firmed more than five percent or 250 forints to end at 4,950. Meat processor Pick rose one percent or 110 forints to end at 11,110, but it had slack volume of 5,200 stocks.

The pharmaceuticals issues finished mixed. Egis gained nearly three percent to end at 10,035 forints but its wolume was meagre. Richter dropped 140 fornts to end at 10,960, while Human remained steady at 3,000.

Traders said that after a strong rally in January and in the first half of February, which saw the BUX index to peak at 5,815.38 points on February 5 from 4,134.31 at the end of 1996, the stock exchange was expected to be in a resting period.
"The index will hover around 5,000 points without dramatic changes," said Bathory.

"It's obvious that U.S. market expectations, namely a possible interest rate increase and the dollar's movements will substantially influence this (the BUX's changes), but these events are independent from the companies and from the country's (Hungary's) rating," the Creditanstalt trader added.
Baranyai had a similar view on the market's near-term outlook, saying that the bourse will not divert substantially from its current path.
"I expect this rangebound trading to remain and I expect some falls within a few days," Gog's trader said.
